old: A 1976 Swiss 5-franc coin. The front shows the head of an alpine herdsman; the back shows the Swiss cross shield and 5 FR. inside an alpine wreath. Designed by Paul Burkhard and struck in copper-nickel (75% copper, 25% nickel).

old: A Japanese 10 yen in bronze, dated Heisei 19 (2007), the nineteenth year of Emperor Akihito's reign. One side shows the Phoenix Hall of Byodoin temple in Uji, a thousand-year-old building so loved that it also appears on the 10,000 yen note. The other side frames a big 10 in a wreath of evergreen leaves. Japan has struck this design, nearly unchanged, since 1951, and it is still the 10 yen in everyday pockets today. The collection already holds two Showa-era strikes of the same design from 1982 and 1988; this is its first Heisei one.
new: A Japanese 10 yen in bronze, dated Heisei 14 (2002), the fourteenth year of Emperor Akihito's reign. One side shows the Phoenix Hall of Byodoin temple in Uji, a thousand-year-old building whose rooftop phoenix statue also appeared on the 10,000 yen note. The other side frames a big 10 in a wreath of evergreen leaves. Japan has struck this design, nearly unchanged, since 1951, and it is still the 10 yen in everyday pockets today. The collection already holds two Showa-era strikes of the same design from 1982 and 1988; this is its first Heisei one.
source: checked against https://en.numista.com/catalogue/pieces3047.html, https://www.npb.go.jp/en/products/intro/kihon.html, and https://www.byodoin.or.jp/en/learn/sculpture/: Sentence 1 had Heisei 19 (2007) / nineteenth year instead of the record's Heisei 14 (2002) / fourteenth year (confirmed in Numista N#3047 year table, 平成十四年); Sentence 2 said the Phoenix Hall building itself appears on the 10,000 yen note, whereas the Series E 10,000 yen note (2004-2024) depicts the rooftop phoenix statue from Phoenix Hall. All other claims hold.
